name: Registered Item Model
title: Base RDF/OWL and SHACL model for register items and register governance
abstract: A base RDF and SHACL model for register items, register item classes and register governance metadata, based on ISO 19135:2026.
description: A register is a catalogue distinguished from a plain dataset by systematic governance: a content information model (register item classes and register items) plus management metadata (identifiers, statuses, actions, roles). ISO 19135:2026 defines one such model, separating a concept plane (meaning) from a content plane (representation) and adding roles, statuses, actions, relations and commitments on top. This block publishes that model as a single base building block so that many registers with different native schemas — a CSV catalogue, the OGC Definitions Server, a GitHub-managed vocabulary, or a Building Blocks register itself — can each map their own fields onto it via a JSON-LD context, and be queried as one graph. Sub-registers are expected to profile this block (null, additive or constrained) rather than invent their own register model.

sources.title: ISO 19135:2026, Geographic information — Registration and register governance
Registers and register governance for federated semantic resources (companion analysis)

examples.title: A governed concept register
examples.content:
A national vocabulary register for plant taxa: it maintains both a concept plane
(the taxon as a unit of meaning) and a content plane (the register item that
represents it), assigns all six governance roles, and records the action and
change classification behind a status change. This is the pattern a "governed
concept register" (the second-most capable of the five ISO 19135:2026 register
types) maps onto.

examples.title: A minimal content register item
examples.content:
The lightest of the five ISO 19135:2026 conformant register types — a "content
register" — has no concept plane and no governance requirements class. A register
item still needs only what the base block requires: an item class, an object
identifier, and validity and publication status.
